name: flipflop
short: Pairs your devices once, then lets any of them send files, links or text to the others over Bluetooth, LAN or the internet.
what: flipflop sets up a trusted tunnel between two or more devices. After that, one device can send files to another at any time, nearby or far away. It's built on Iroh.
who: Anyone who moves files, links or notes between their own devices, or a family's devices. There's no iOS build, so iPhone users can't use it.
needs: A Linux, macOS, Windows or Android device on each end
For building from source: Rust with `cargo`, and for Android, `just`, `cargo-apk`, the Android SDK and NDK

steps.title: Download a build
steps.text: Get the latest Linux, macOS or Windows build or the Android APK from the releases page at github.com/andunieee/flipflop/releases/latest. On Windows, run the executable directly or use the `-setup.exe` installer.

steps.title: Or build it yourself
steps.text: The first line builds the desktop app and the second installs on Android.
steps.code:
cargo run --release          # desktop
just android-install         # Android (needs cargo-apk, Android SDK + NDK)

try.label: From the README
try.text: Set up a tunnel between your laptop and your phone, then send a link or some plain text from one to the other.

watch: Windows shows a "Windows protected your PC" warning when you run it, according to the README.
The README is short and doesn't explain pairing or security in detail, so expect to work some things out in the app.
